Platform-specific font metrics for the placeholder/secure-text leading to different dot density.
Header component uses absolute or fixed sizing that scales differently on iOS viewport (1170×2532 vs 390×844 dp).

summary: iOS shows the iOS software keyboard occupying the lower half of the screen, while Android has no keyboard visible — the composer area is fully empty on Android.

Body text 'Review the Android composer crop' appears slightly larger / heavier on iOS compared to Android; character glyphs render with iOS San Francisco metrics (taller x-height, tighter letter spacing) vs Android Roboto.

Header tag pill on iOS reads 'IOS' (caps) instead of 'ANDROID'; badge text weight and color are consistent across platforms, but the label differs as expected.
likelyCauses: Kuikly input/composer focus state is being triggered on iOS but not on Android, causing the iOS system keyboard to attach to the focused TextField while Android's IME is suppressed or not opened.

Native keyboard insets are not being applied consistently, so the layout below the composer is not adjusted on Android the way it is on iOS.
suggestedFixes: Make the focus/IME invocation deterministic on both ends: explicitly call requestFocus and requestKeyboard on mount, or guard it so neither auto-opens during visual baseline capture.
Apply KeyboardAvoidingView / safe-area-inset-keyboard uniformly so the composer reflows the same way on both platforms.

Normalize the body text fontFamily to a Kuikly-mapped token so San Francisco vs Roboto differences do not shift metrics during comparison.
intentional: Different header pill label text ('IOS' vs 'ANDROID') is a deliberate platform marker and should not be treated as a regression.

intentional: Pink selection highlight on the active 'design' suggestion appears intentional and is consistent across both platforms.

suggestedFixes: Normalize the screenshot capture to dismiss the iOS keyboard (or apply `IME`-aware layout) before capturing so both ends compare the same chrome-free state.

intentional: Showing the iOS keyboard in the screenshot is likely a capture artifact rather than an intentional product difference.

Android menu has 7 items including a 'Select Text' entry plus an extra 'Follow Thread' on React that becomes its own grouped section; React shows 7 items with 'Select Message' and no 'Select Text'.

React groups emoji reactions inside the popover and places Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Message in one block, then Open Thread/Save Message/Follow Thread in another; Android splits Copy Link/Copy Markdown/Select Text/Select Message into a single block and Open Thread/Save Message into another, with Convert to Task isolated.

Different component primitive used on Android (Card/OutlinedButton rows vs. React's Menu/Popover), producing mismatched paddings, dividers, and font metrics.
Token mismatch for spacing/radius/elevation between design system web and Compose themes.

summary: Selection action bar position differs: React renders the yellow toolbar at the bottom of the viewport (~y=2380), Android renders it inline just below the second message (~y=470).

likelyCauses: Android implementation renders the selection toolbar as an inline component attached to the last selected item rather than a sticky bottom toolbar.

Unify the action button set: expose Cancel, Forward/Send, Copy, and Overflow (or All + Forward) consistently across platforms; remove the Android-only download icon or align its semantics.
Render the message-selection checkbox as a leading column (filled circle with check) rather than overlaying the avatar tile.
Restore the per-message reaction row (👍 count and + button) under messages on Android to match React.
Use identical seed/fixture data in both visual baselines so only real layout deltas are measured.

summary: Timestamp text differs: React shows '17 days ago'/'20 days ago'/'20 days ago' while Android shows '14 days ago'/'16 days ago'/'16 days ago' — likely a data snapshot/fixture mismatch, not a styling issue.
Spacing between the tab row ('All / Unread / Mentions') and 'Mark all read' button is tighter on Android; the filter row sits closer to the dividing line on the right side.
Vertical spacing between activity cards is larger on Android, causing the list to start lower and end with more empty space at the bottom.
The '@Cindy' card body text on Android uses a smaller font size and appears more compact, while React renders the Chinese characters at a noticeably larger weight.
Tab buttons ('All','Unread','Mentions') appear slightly narrower on Android with reduced internal horizontal padding, making the yellow 'All' chip smaller.
likelyCauses: Activity card timestamp rendered from different fixture snapshots between platforms
Android Compose implementation using different list item padding/density defaults than the React baseline
Android theming overrides tab control min-height and chip padding
Font scaling/sp values on Android diverge from React's rem/px sizing for card body text
suggestedFixes: Align the activity feed fixture so both platforms render identical relative timestamps (or freeze a deterministic date).
Match Android card vertical spacing to the React values (increase outer card padding or row gap to match the ~28px React rhythm).
Adjust Android tab/chip dimensions (minHeight, horizontal padding) to match React baseline widths.
Reconcile font sizes for card body content (e.g., the 'Cindy:' line) so Android scales match React's text-sm/lg tokens.
Verify the bottom whitespace — if intentional, mark as accepted variance; if not, tighten card padding or reduce inter-card gap on Android.
intentional: Different absolute 'days ago' values likely intentional if using a live data source, but should be normalized for visual regression baselines

summary: Body and metadata text in cards uses a heavier/bolder font weight on iOS compared to React baseline
First card body text is truncated with ellipsis ('…') on React but wraps fully on iOS (no ellipsis)
Day-ago counters differ: React shows '17 days ago' / '20 days ago' / '20 days ago', iOS shows '14 days ago' / '16 days ago' / '16 days ago'
iOS list is more vertically compact: cards have less inner padding and smaller vertical spacing between cards
Card 3 (@Cindy / '201继续推进') content occupies less vertical space on iOS, with reduced line-height
likelyCauses: Different default font weight/scale on iOS (UIFont) vs web (system sans-serif) fallback
Truncation/line-clamp rule applied on React (e.g., CSS -webkit-line-clamp or maxLines) not mirrored on iOS
Relative timestamps rendered from different 'now' references (date math or stale snapshot)
Card padding/margin tokens not shared across platforms — iOS uses tighter design system spacing
iOS host view lacks bottom safe-area inset / scroll content insets, causing tighter bottom alignment
suggestedFixes: Align iOS card text font weight/leading to match React typography scale (e.g., map to UIFontMetrics-compatible styles)
Apply the same line-clamp/maxLines on the body in iOS so truncation matches React
Use a shared relative-time util so 'days ago' values are computed consistently
Share spacing tokens (card padding, vertical gap) between React and iOS implementations
Confirm card height/min-height tokens so cards render equal height across platforms

summary: Card 1 (#design) on iOS shows full text '#product:f8e569cb' while Android truncates with ellipsis ('#product:f8e569cb…').
Card 1 secondary line on iOS shows full text 'Review the Android composer crop' while Android truncates with ellipsis ('Review the Android composer cro…').
Card 1 content area on iOS occupies more vertical space (no ellipsis) versus Android's compressed/truncated layout, causing the card body to be taller.
iOS rendering has more available horizontal width inside cards, allowing two extra words before truncation, while Android's narrower effective width forces earlier ellipsis.
Layout density differs: Android packs cards tighter vertically due to truncation, iOS cards are slightly taller with full text rendering.
likelyCauses: Different default text container widths between Android and iOS Kuikly renderers (likely DP-to-pt conversion or padding discrepancies).

Missing or inconsistent `maxLines`/ellipsize behavior in the card title and body Text components — iOS may be ignoring overflow constraints while Android enforces them, or vice versa with different available width.
Inconsistent horizontal padding or margin values applied to card content on the two platforms.
Different font metrics (system font on iOS vs Roboto on Android) causing line-break thresholds to differ even at the same nominal DP size.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Kuikly cross-platform UI / Activity Results component owner
suggestedFixes: Normalize card content padding and ensure identical horizontal insets on Android and iOS.
Verify `maxLines` and `overflow` (ellipsis) are explicitly set on both card title and body Text components so truncation matches across platforms.
Use `numberOfLines` consistently and test with the widest expected content to guarantee single-platform truncation parity.
Audit the Kuikly text layout bridge to confirm measured width and font metrics are equivalent between Android (DP) and iOS (pt).
Add a visual regression check for the truncated vs full-text card states on both platforms.
intentional: Platform system font rendering differences (iOS SF vs Android Roboto) at the glyph level
iOS home indicator bar visible at bottom is an expected platform chrome element
Top breadcrumb/metadata bar differences are part of Slock's comparison harness, not the app under test

cases.title: Tasks Panel States

summary: Android header shows a square checkbox icon to the left of the 'Tasks' title; React header has no icon.

Task card vertical density is higher on Android — all four status sections (TODO, IN PROGRESS, IN REVIEW, DONE) fit on one canvas, while React scrolls with more spacing per card and crops the last card's status badge.
React card bodies have noticeably more vertical padding between the metadata row and the title; Android cards are more compact.
React's TODO column count badge ('1') sits further right of the orange TODO pill with a wider gap; Android uses a tighter inline spacing.
likelyCauses: Android header component renders a leading checkbox/list icon by default that React's header omits.
Android task card uses a denser spacing scale (smaller vertical paddings) than React's card spacing tokens.
React list may apply extra section header height or larger card min-height from a different layout primitive.
suggestedFixes: Decide whether the header checkbox icon should be shared; if yes, add it to React's Tasks header; if platform-only, document as intentional.
Align task card vertical padding and section spacing between Android and React using the shared spacing tokens.
Normalize the column header (pill + count) inline gap to the same value across platforms.
If the React panel is intentionally scrollable at this height, ensure the card density matches so content fits comparably or confirm intentional density difference.
intentional: Android task card top-right timestamp (relative format) — react-adopts-later per artin 2026-07-06.
Android task card bottom-left assignee line ('Unassigned' / '@name') — react-adopts-later per artin 2026-07-06.
Filter chip row (Channel/Creator/Assignee) present on Android in a single-row layout vs React's wrapped layout — platform-difference, must not be 'fixed'.

summary: Filter chip row layout differs: React wraps to two rows (#, Creator on row 1; Assignee on row 2), iOS fits all three on a single row — intentional platform difference per spec.
iOS task cards include top-right timestamp (e.g. 20:24, 06-22 10:30) and bottom-left assignee line (Unassigned, @Cindy, @Product UX Designer); React cards omit both — react-adopts-later per spec.
iOS header includes a square checkbox-with-check icon to the left of the 'Tasks' title; React header has no such icon, leaving the title left-aligned with extra whitespace.
likelyCauses: React task card component not yet wired to render relative timestamp or assignee metadata (tracked adoption).
React header does not render the decorative/affordance checkbox glyph present on iOS.
React filter chip container uses a wrapping flex layout instead of iOS's single-row horizontally scrollable row (platform-spec difference, not a bug).
suggestedFixes: Add per-card top-right relative timestamp and bottom-left assignee line to the React task card (tracked under task #373).
Optionally add the leading checkbox icon in the React Tasks header for visual parity with iOS.
Leave the React filter chip wrapped layout as-is; this is an intentional platform divergence.
intentional: Filter chip row: React two-row wrap vs iOS single-row is an intentional platform-difference and must not be 'fixed'.
Per-card top-right timestamp and bottom-left assignee line are react-adopts-later; iOS behavior is the desired product feature, not a defect.

summary: Menu trigger pill ("In Progress" with edit/pencil icon) and dropdown panel render with matching structure, colors, border weight, and item order on both Android and iOS.

No clipping, missing elements, or misalignment of the menu container between the two renders.
likelyCauses: Minor sub-pixel/anti-aliasing differences in text and icon edges, consistent with the 0.87% pixel mismatch and ~94% RGB similarity.
Slight canvas scaling/resampling difference due to very different raw canvas sizes (342×260 vs 1170×2532) before component crop.
Platform-default text shaping differences (Roboto vs San Francisco) producing marginal glyph metrics within the 1dp layout tolerance.
suggestedFixes: Treat the remaining delta as cosmetic; no action required given 99.13% pixel-perfect similarity.
If a stricter match is desired, normalize text to a single platform-agnostic font (e.g., shared webfont) used identically on Android and iOS Kuikly builds.
Confirm the layoutDp tolerance of 1dp is intentional in the Slock config for this component to avoid future flaky diffs.
Optionally re-crop both ends to identical component bounds (baseline currently uses manual-rect, iOS has no crop) to reduce empty-canvas noise in the metric.
intentional: Identical trigger pill color (cyan) and identical dropdown panel border/shadow style on both platforms.

cases.title: Home Create Channel Dialog

summary: Android version uses more vertical space, pushing VISIBILITY, MEMBERS, AGENTS, and HUMANS sections lower and expanding the dialog to nearly fill the viewport while React version is more compact.

Description field on Android renders as a single-line input instead of a multi-line textarea; placeholder text "Build reports, screenshots, release" is clipped/truncated with no wrap (React wraps to two lines and shows a resize handle).
Agent and human list rows on Android include a secondary meta line (e.g. "agent · @Cindy", "human · @designer") that is absent in React rows, increasing row height and adding avatars+text per item.
Spacing between form sections (label-to-input, input-to-label) is larger on Android, especially around VISIBILITY and MEMBERS.
The pink checkmark indicators for selected members are present on both but are positioned differently due to row-height change; Android checks sit further right within taller rows.
likelyCauses: Android implementation maps the Description field to a single-line TextInput instead of a multi-line TextArea.
Android Member/Agent list item template renders two lines (primary name + secondary handle/role) vs React's single-line template.
Android applies larger vertical padding/margin on form labels, inputs, and list rows than the React design tokens specify.
Dialog body on Android uses fillViewportHeight or wrapContent with extra padding, while React constrains dialog height to content.
suggestedFixes: Replace the single-line EditText for Description with a multi-line input (inputType="textMultiLine") and minLines/tall enough to show wrapped placeholder text.
Reduce member list row template on Android to a single primary line (or make the secondary meta line optional/hidden by default) to match React row height.
Normalize vertical spacing tokens (label margin, input height, section gap) to match React values; audit dimens.xml for form spacing.
Constrain the Android dialog max height so it doesn't fill the viewport when content is short, or apply scrolling inside the dialog body.
Verify the pink selection checkmark alignment still reads correctly after row-height normalization.
intentional: Pink "Create Channel" primary button color and selected-member row tint appear consistent across both platforms.

summary: iOS render is clipped/cropped by the on-screen keyboard: AGENTS section, Cancel, and Create Channel buttons are hidden while React baseline shows the full dialog including action buttons.

Dialog vertical layout is significantly compressed on iOS—VISIBILITY, MEMBERS, and AGENTS sections are pushed up and overlap with the keyboard region, whereas React renders at full height with comfortable spacing.
iOS shows an active text caret in the Name field (editing state); React baseline shows the field without focus/caret, indicating state/initial vs. editing mismatch.
Submit/Create and Cancel CTAs are missing from the iOS view due to keyboard occlusion; React baseline shows both buttons clearly at the bottom.
likelyCauses: iOS keyboard not accounted for in the dialog's safe-area / contentInset behavior, causing the modal to remain anchored to the viewport instead of insetting when the keyboard appears.
Missing keyboardAvoidingView / safe-area padding equivalent in the iOS implementation of the create-channel modal.

cases.title: Settings Notifications Page

summary: React shows a single 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' section with web-push explanation, 'UNAVAILABLE' status, 'Enable Push Notifications' CTA (pink/disabled), and 'Mute this server' with checkbox + Save button.

Android shows a materially different, OS-level notifications control surface: 'Notification permission / Allowed' panel, 'Enabled/Disabled' toggle, 'Keep alive / Normal' toggle, 'Manage notifications' deep link, 'Test notification / Ready' panel, and 'Workspace mute / Unmuted/Muted' toggle.
React layout is compact (~half the viewport) and padded at top; Android layout fills more vertical space with multiple stacked cards/groups.
Header row (back arrow + 'Notifications' title + divider) is visually consistent across both sides.
React uses a muted/disabled pink button affordance for 'Enable Push Notifications' and 'Save'; Android uses yellow-highlighted button states with outlined (filled white) buttons for primary actions.
likelyCauses: React (web) uses Web Push API which is unavailable in the test browser, so the page renders the web-push fallback state with 'UNAVAILABLE' banner and disabled CTA.

Android uses platform-native APIs (NotificationManager, foreground services, system channels) and exposes OS-level controls (permission panel, tray notifications, keep-alive, manage-in-system, workspace mute) that don't exist on web.
The same Settings page is implemented as two separate platform-specific surfaces rather than a single cross-platform component, leading to divergent copy and control sets.
Crop mismatch (component-bounds vs viewport-bounds) inflates pixel mismatch beyond what is caused by UI alone.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Platform notifications / settings feature owner (mobile + web)
suggestedFixes: Confirm whether the divergence is intentional: if Android should expose OS-level settings (permission, tray, keep-alive, manage, test, workspace mute) and web should expose web-push equivalents, mark the page as platform-acceptable and adjust tolerances or comparison contract accordingly.
Normalize crop contracts: switch both sides to viewport-bounds (or both to component-bounds) so Slock isn't comparing an element-cropped React frame against a full-frame Android shot.
Add a shared spec for the Notifications page that lists required controls per platform; if a control only exists on one platform, document it in component metadata so visual tests don't flag it.

On the web side, redesign the 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' empty/unavailable state to still match the card/divider structure used on Android (e.g., outlined cards with consistent padding) so layout pattern is comparable.
Ensure disabled-button styling is consistent: React uses pink/disabled whereas Android uses yellow-outlined — align the design tokens for 'primary disabled' across platforms.
intentional: React 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' unavailable state is a legitimate web platform fallback.
Android 'Notification permission / Allowed' panel and 'Manage notifications' deep link are OS-level affordances unique to mobile.
Android 'Keep alive / Normal' toggle corresponds to a foreground service behavior that does not exist on web.
'Workspace mute / Unmuted / Muted' on Android is a native mute affordance and may not have an exact web equivalent.

summary: React shows a single combined push-notifications card with UNVAVAILABLE badge and an 'Enable Push Notifications' button; iOS breaks the same area into five distinct rows: 'Show system notifications', 'Notification permission / Request permission', 'Enabled/Disabled' toggle, 'Keep alive/Normal' toggle, and 'Test notification / Ready'.
iOS adds an extra bottom section 'Workspace mute' with Unmuted/Muted toggle that is absent on React.
React uses an inline checkbox + 'Save' button pattern ('Mute this server'); iOS uses a toggle-button pair (Unmuted/Muted) without checkbox or Save.

Primary action button styling differs: React shows a pink-filled CTA ('Enable Push Notifications') and pink Save button; iOS uses yellow-filled toggle buttons (Enabled, Normal, Unmuted, Ready) with black borders.
Status pills diverge in copy and color: React shows a yellow 'UNAVAILABLE' pill; iOS uses no equivalent status pill, instead displaying 'Allowed' as subdued text under 'Notification permission'.
likelyCauses: Platform divergent implementation: iOS version was rebuilt with iOS-native toggles and an additional Workspace mute section while React kept the original single-card layout.
Design parity gap: settings notifications page spec was only partially shared with the iOS team, leading to a superset of controls on iOS.
Push-notification flow differs per platform (web push vs OS-level permission), so iOS exposes 'Request permission', 'Keep alive', and 'Test notification' rows that React cannot.
Mute control migrated from checkbox+Save form (web) to immediate toggle (mobile), but review for parity was missed.
suggestedFixes: Align both platforms on a shared settings schema: same set of notification controls (show, permission, enable/disable, keep-alive, test, workspace mute) in the same order, then implement platform-appropriate widgets.
Replace React's checkbox+Save with an immediate 'Unmuted/Muted' toggle pair to match iOS, or alternatively hide the iOS Workspace mute row until parity is confirmed.
Move the status indicator to a consistent component: yellow 'StatusPill' should appear on iOS where 'Allowed/Denied' text currently shows (and vice-versa).
Standardize section header treatment: either keep 'PUSH NOTIFICATIONS' uppercase label on both, or drop it on both and rely on row titles only.
Audit CTA colors: confirm pink-fill vs yellow-fill primary action palette is intentional per platform; if not, align to a single accent color.
intentional: Workspace mute section may be intentionally mobile-only because the web client already has a global mute elsewhere.
iOS keeps an explicit OS-level 'Request permission' action because iOS notifications require user authorization, while web push can be enabled in-browser site settings.

summary: Header label 'Notifications' on iOS appears bolder/heavier than on Android.
Description body text (e.g., 'System notification permission is granted.', 'Show a system tray notification...', 'Keep realtime connected...') appears slightly thicker/bolder on iOS vs Android.
Toggle pill sizing is consistent, but spacing between 'Keep alive'/'Normal' buttons is tighter on iOS, causing them to appear nearly touching while Android has a clear gap.
Vertical rhythm/section gaps appear marginally compressed on iOS (lines and dividers sit closer together than on Android).
Manage notifications button on iOS extends closer to the right edge with less right padding than on Android.
likelyCauses: Default font weight differences between iOS SF and Android Roboto when no explicit fontWeight is set.
Absence of an explicit font-family/fontWeight in the Kuikly shared style, letting each platform fall back to its native default.
Platform-specific text metrics causing different line-height wrapping inside the permission description block.
Minor density scale divergence (e.g., 8pt grid vs iOS points) producing tighter component paddings on iOS.
suggestedFixes: Pin an explicit fontFamily and fontWeight for body and header text on both ends to neutralize platform font fallbacks.
Normalize line-height (e.g., set an explicit multiplier or dp value) on the description labels so wrapping matches across platforms.
Standardize spacing scale tokens (gap, padding) used by toggle pills and buttons; verify on Android 390dp and iOS 1170px canvases.
Add an explicit right padding to the 'Manage notifications' button container so both platforms reserve the same trailing whitespace.
Re-run the slock diff after token alignment; expect RGB similarity to rise above 0.95 and pixel mismatch to drop below 0.05.

summary: Different layout density: Android uses a more compact, stacked layout with merged/shorter section headers, while React uses larger, separated cards with more whitespace.

Section header style differs: React shows 'CONNECTED APPS' and 'BUILT-IN' as small uppercase labels in muted color above cards; Android replaces these with inline section icons and titles ('Connected Apps', 'Built-in') plus subtitle text under the page title.

Counter/pill representation differs: React renders 'Marketplace 3 / Installed 2 / My apps 1' as combined labeled pills; Android splits these into separate numeric tiles ('3', '2', '1') with labels beneath, then a secondary row of icon-prefixed tabs.

App card action button variant differs: React 'Open' button is solid pink with no icon; Android 'Open' button adds an external-link icon next to the label. 'Install' (React) vs 'Details' (Android) labels differ for the same card slot.

Iconography and typography weight: Android uses outlined leading icons (link, store, check, key) and lighter body type for descriptions; React uses plain bordered tiles with bold titles and no leading icons.
likelyCauses: Different component libraries / design-system implementations between web (React) and native (Android) targets producing divergent visual defaults.
Independent re-implementation of the Connected Apps page in Android rather than shared design tokens, leading to restructured information hierarchy.
Varied interpretation of spec for counter/pill groupings and section labeling.
suggestedFixes: Define and share a single visual contract (tokens) for section labels, counter pills, and card actions across React and Android implementations.
Unify header treatment: decide whether a subtitle under 'Connected Apps' belongs in both platforms and render consistently.
Standardize the numeric counters (Marketplace/Installed/My apps) — either as combined pills (React) or as numeric tiles (Android) — and apply the chosen pattern everywhere.
Align action buttons on app cards: same label semantics ('Open' vs 'Details' vs 'Install') and same icon usage across platforms.
Match search input styling: include or omit the leading search icon consistently and unify placeholder text casing/ellipsis.
intentional: Platform-native density conventions may justify the more compact Android layout and added icons.

The yellow inline-code fill on iOS bleeds across whitespace between adjacent code spans (e.g., 'inlineCode' and 'go test ./...' and 'git commit -s' appear to share a single continuous yellow box), whereas React keeps each code span as a separate bordered chip.

Header metadata row differs: iOS shows the avatar, name, and a truncated 'Keeps visual testing…' subtitle on one line with the timestamp appended, while React stacks the avatar/name line and uses a more compact, two-line header with 'Keeps vis…' truncation and the timestamp on its own sub-line; vertical alignment of the avatar relative to the name differs slightly between the two.

Body text wrapping on iOS causes the long inline-code path to overflow the right edge of the container (final glyphs clip at the container border) instead of breaking cleanly inside the chip like React does.
likelyCauses: iOS text engine uses a larger default body font size or line-height multiplier than the React baseline.
iOS TextKit/UIKit wraps inline-code chips on a per-glyph basis and omits the trailing border on continuation lines, and may merge backgrounds of adjacent inline spans separated by spaces.
Missing or different `word-break`/`overflow-wrap` settings for inline code in iOS markdown renderer, allowing tokens to exceed container width instead of soft-wrapping mid-token.
iOS message row header layout uses a single-line HStack rather than the multi-line header layout in React, changing avatar/name/timestamp stacking.
suggestedFixes: Set iOS body font size and line-height to match React's MessageItem body metrics (verify against the 390×844 baseline).
Fix inline-code chip rendering on iOS to (a) preserve the black right/bottom border on each wrap line and (b) not merge backgrounds across whitespace-separated spans.
Add `overflow-wrap: anywhere` (or equivalent `lineBreakMode`/hyphenation setting) to inline-code runs so long tokens wrap inside the chip rather than clipping at the container edge.
Align the message-row header layout between platforms so avatar/name and timestamp/subtitle stack consistently.

cases.title: Settings Administration Full Height Screen

summary: Android renders a full top app bar with back arrow and 'Administration' title that is absent on the React baseline.

Android displays more vertical sections (System Channels, Pending Invites, Join Links, Pre-Join Agreement, Onboarding, Translation, Member Permissions, Sidebar Order, Danger Zone) with distinct card-based groupings versus React's flat single-column form layout.

React uses pink/red filled primary buttons (Update Role, Save, Create Invite Link) while Android replaces them with yellow/gold accent buttons and outline-style action chips (Required/Disabled, Yes/No, Hide Humans/Visible).

React shows form inputs as native dropdowns (Select member..., Admin, @cindy (Cindy)) with mm/dd/yyyy date input; Android renders information as labeled rows with leading icon tiles and 'Unavailable'/'Last owner' status text on the right.
Character counter on Android ('81/5000 characters') and Preview block placement differ from React's preview rendering and placement of '81/5000' inline under textarea.
likelyCauses: React baseline and Android implementation diverge from a shared design system; Android is using a newer visual language (tile-based cards, yellow accent, monospace metadata) not reflected in React's flat form.
Primary button color token mismatch: React uses destructive/pink, Android uses brand yellow.
State indicators (toggle on/off, required/disabled) implemented as pill chips on Android vs. checkboxes on React, indicating inconsistent component mapping.
Section grouping on Android uses cards with headers while React relies on whitespace separators.
Header/navigation component (app bar with back arrow) is present in Android native shell but missing from React web render.
suggestedFixes: Reconcile section header style and grouping (cards vs. flat) across platforms; align typography weight, size, and uppercase tracking.
Standardize primary action button color token; pick pink or yellow as the canonical primary and update the other platform.
Unify state indicator components: map React checkboxes to Android toggle pills consistently and share the same active/inactive styling.
Add the top app bar with back navigation to the React web Administration screen to match Android.
Normalize Pending Invites row metadata (Invited by, timestamps) and action button placement.
intentional: Different overall canvas height (2564 vs 2647) likely reflects native scrollbar/status bar differences and may be acceptable.

cases.title: Settings Connected Apps Full Height Screen

summary: Header structure differs: React uses 'CONNECTED APPS' label with link icon on the left; Android uses a back arrow plus 'Connected Apps' title bar with a separate breadcrumb row beneath.
Experimental tag placement differs: React shows it in the header near the title; Android shows it inside the description card below the body text.

'Register app' button position and shape differ: React shows it inline in the header area; Android places it floating to the right of the 'Third-party apps for this server' heading, partially overlapping the card edge.

Tab layout inverts: React shows pill-style tabs (Marketplace 3, Installed 2, My apps 1) inside the description card; Android shows them as separate navigation tabs/icons (Marketplace, Installed, My Apps) below the card, then duplicates the stat tiles inside the card.
Section icons missing in React: Android adds a package icon next to 'Built-in' and a storefront icon next to 'Marketplace' that do not exist on the React side.
likelyCauses: Independent redesign of the Connected Apps page in the Android app rather than parity with the React baseline.
Different design system tokens (spacing, radius, typography weight) applied across platforms.
Component-level divergence: avatar tiles, status pills, and category badges not implemented in the Android variant.
Tab/segmented control was refactored into a bottom tab bar on Android with redundant stat tiles kept inside the description card.
The 'Register app' call-to-action was promoted to a prominent position in Android, causing it to overlap or sit beside the section heading.
analysis.suggestedOwner: Android / Connected Apps feature team (cross-platform design parity owner)
suggestedFixes: Align Android header with React: use a 'CONNECTED APPS' label + link icon row, and place the EXPERIMENTAL tag adjacent to the title (not inside the body card).
Move 'Register app' to a header-right button matching React position and remove overlap with the 'Third-party apps for this server' heading.
Reconcile the tab strip: keep one set of tabs (icon + label + count) and remove the duplicate stat tile row inside the description card on Android.
Add the package and storefront icons to the React side (or remove them from Android) to match section iconography across platforms.
Restore avatar tiles, category pills, and INSTALLED/Install action buttons on the Android app list rows, or simplify React to match the compact Details-only row.
intentional: The back-arrow + 'Connected Apps' title bar on Android is a platform-conventional navigation pattern and may be intentional for mobile UX.
Adding icons next to section headers (Built-in, Marketplace) on Android may be an intentional information-density improvement for smaller screens.
